    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Industry observers note that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Sources indicate that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    Industry observers note that if PCE highlights inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    It has been revealed that I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index indicated wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    In a recent development, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a newly introduced home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    What Security Teams Still Get Wrong About Asset Visibility

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1030 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Yochai Corem is GM of Exposure Management at Check Point Software.
    • Organizations have more asset data than ever, but turning that data into a reliable view of what they own, operate and expose remains difficult.
    • In a recent development, A server appears in three tools with different identifiers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Yochai Corem is GM of Exposure Management at Check Point Software.

    Organizations have more asset data than ever, but turning that data into a reliable view of what they own, operate and expose remains difficult.

    In a recent development, A server appears in three tools with different identifiers. A cloud workload has an owner who has left the business. A forgotten website remains online after the campaign that funded it has ended. Each leaves security teams with information they still have to investigate before they can act.

    According to recent reports, security leaders should judge asset visibility by how reliably it supports a decision. A useful inventory helps teams establish what an asset does, who is responsible for it, how it is protected and what should happen when a problem appears.

    Several familiar assumptions prevent organizations from reaching that standard.

    An incomplete configuration management database (CMDB) should prompt a review of how records are created, updated and retired.

    Sources indicate that start by defining its purpose. The CMDB should record the systems, services and dependencies needed to manage business operations, with accountable owners and lifecycle status. Detailed security telemetry can remain in specialist systems, linked through reliable identifiers. An impersonating website belongs in an external threat register connected to the affected brand.

    Sources indicate that then identify which sources can reveal missing records. Cloud platforms, endpoint management, identity providers, vulnerability scanners and procurement systems can each expose inconsistencies. Buying a service should trigger registration; retiring it should trigger checks that access, infrastructure and records have been removed.

    According to recent reports, reconciliation should reflect the pace of change. I would set a daily reconciliation target for cloud and endpoint feeds; use deployment and retirement events to trigger updates; and review unresolved discrepancies weekly. Quarterly ownership reviews can supplement those checks.

    An asset without an owner needs an interim accountable team and an escalation deadline. “Unknown” should describe an investigation in progress.

    The modern attack surface spans internal infrastructure, cloud workloads, software as a service (SaaS), internet-facing systems, supplier connections and the organization’s broader digital presence.

    Recent findings suggest that those categories need different forms of accountability. Infrastructure teams may manage servers, cloud teams manage workloads and business application owners sponsor SaaS services. Marketing or regional teams may control domains and social accounts. Supplier relationships require a business sponsor alongside technical oversight.

    According to recent reports, security should establish a review and response process across those boundaries. A newly discovered domain needs ownership verification and an assessment of what it hosts. An unfamiliar SaaS service needs checks on its users, data and access. A fraudulent social account needs investigation and a disruption process.

    Recent findings suggest that review frequency should follow exposure and change, with continuous discovery where practical and scheduled reviews for ownership, supplier access and dormant services. This broader scope aligns with the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST) inclusion of hardware, software, services and supplier services in asset management.

    Leaders can test this assumption by following a newly discovered asset through the security process.

    Industry observers note that does discovery trigger checks for required endpoint protection, vulnerability scanning and an accountable owner? Does an unmanaged internet-facing system reach someone authorized to restrict or remove it? Can the organization confirm that the resulting action occurred?

    These outcomes show whether visibility operates as a security control. The Center for Internet Security’s (CIS) Control 1 connects inventory management with identifying and addressing unauthorized or unmanaged assets.

    In a recent development, useful measures include the time taken to assign ownership, the proportion of applicable assets covered by required controls and the age of unresolved discrepancies. A growing inventory count provides little reassurance when newly discovered systems remain unmanaged.

    Additional tools introduce additional records, each with its own identifiers, timestamps and assumptions.

    Effective reconciliation requires explicit rules. Stable cloud resource identifiers or device identifiers should take precedence over an Internet Protocol (IP) address that may change or be reused. Records need source and freshness information so teams can distinguish a current observation from a stale entry.

    Organizations also need rules for conflicting fields. The identity system may establish who uses a device, while a service registry identifies the team accountable for the application it supports. Those relationships should remain distinguishable.

    According to recent reports, cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM) can support this work. Organizations can also improve CMDB integrations, use cloud asset inventories and service catalogs, or build reconciliation workflows in their existing data platforms. The operational requirements remain consistent: reliable matching, clear authority for each field and a process for resolving exceptions.

    Discovery should initiate a decision about management, protection or retirement.

    In a recent development, A forgotten website needs an owner to confirm whether it still serves a business purpose. A vulnerable application needs assessment of its exposure, dependencies and operational constraints before a response is selected.

    Recent findings suggest that that decision should remain traceable through completion. If a service is retired, verify that it is no longer reachable. If a security control is applied, confirm that it covers the intended asset. Updating the inventory should accompany the operational change.

    This ongoing connection between asset information and action also underpins continuous threat exposure management (CTEM).

    CTEM depends on this discipline throughout scoping, discovery, prioritization, validation and mobilization.

    In a recent development, an unknown asset cannot enter the prioritization process. A known asset without business context is difficult to rank. Missing dependencies weaken assessments of attack paths and change impact. An unknown owner delays action, while stale records undermine confirmation that an exposure has been reduced.

    CAASM and external attack surface management (EASM) can support these stages by reconciling internal records and discovering internet-facing assets. Their value depends on the ownership, decision rules and response processes surrounding them.

    Sources indicate that security leaders should expect asset visibility to connect discovery with accountable action. Every significant asset needs enough current context for someone to determine its protection requirements, address its exposures and verify the result. That is how a reliable inventory helps reduce the opportunities available to an attacker.​.

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1395 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • Recent findings suggest that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • It has been revealed that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Recent findings suggest that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    It has been revealed that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Recent findings suggest that merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    Sources indicate that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    Recent findings suggest that merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    According to recent reports, some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that demonstrates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    According to recent reports, unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    In a recent development, some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    According to recent reports, which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Recent findings suggest that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    According to recent reports, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    Sources indicate that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a significant impact when you add several of them together.

    According to recent reports, understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    Sources indicate that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    #27825. Tech Report: How To Teach Your AI Agent About Your Organization

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (789 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: How To Teach Your AI Agent About Your Organization

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Founder and CEO of Maplith, a company brain for your AI agents.
    • For 16 years, I ran a translation manufacturer that grew from a handful of people into an international business.
    • We had to fetch their files from their own system and deliver them in their own layout, and we could only invoice some of the repetitions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Founder and CEO of Maplith, a company brain for your AI agents.

    For 16 years, I ran a translation manufacturer that grew from a handful of people into an international business. The most important thing I learned about knowledge is that it rarely lives where you think it does.

    One customer shows it well. We had to fetch their files from their own system and deliver them in their own layout, and we could only invoice some of the repetitions. None of that was written down anywhere. It lived with one project manager. Anyone else would have done it the standard way and got it wrong.

    That tailoring was not a side concern. It was the product. If the work had been standard, the customer could have run the model themselves. This is why a firm’s rules never get standardized away: The exceptions are often exactly what customers pay for.

    Sources indicate that I think of this every time someone asks me why their AI agent isn’t delivering. The models are good enough. The problem is that the agent starts from zero every time. It does not know which systems you run, how they connect or which rules you follow without ever writing them down. So it guesses, and a confident guess in your accounts is worse than no answer at all.

    Here are five things you can do this month before you let an agent work inside your business. None of them needs a newly introduced tool.

    Book two hours with the three or four people who make most of the everyday decisions. Ask them one question: “What would a upcoming hire ask you in their first week?” The answers are your unwritten rules: which customers get special terms, when a refund is approved, what can be invoiced and what cannot. Write each one as a short sentence, specific enough to check: “This customer gets files back in their own template.” “Refunds above 300 euros are approved by the finance lead.”.

    List every system you use and what each one is the source of truth for. You will find places where two systems describe the same thing differently. “Returned” in the ERP can mean the customer has sent the item back, while in the warehouse it means the item is back on the shelf.

    Recent findings suggest that the instinct is to make the systems agree. In my experience, that rarely works because each system was set up for the team that uses it, and that is why it works for them. Write the translation down instead. The same goes for numbers. In my manufacturer, the price did not sit in the same place from one customer to the next. Note where it lives for whom and which value to trust for which question.

    According to recent reports, most useful answers need two systems joined: the order in the web shop and the invoice in accounting, or the support ticket and the customer in the CRM. Find the field that ties them together and test it by hand. Take 20 random orders and look for them in the other system. If you find 19, you can build on that link. If you find 12, you cannot, and an agent will rarely tell you it is guessing. The test takes an afternoon and saves months of wrong reports.

    Split actions into four levels: read, propose, act after approval and act alone. Start with everything that changes something requiring approval from a named person. Set limits in money and volume, not in trust. When the agent has proposed the same action a hundred times without a mistake, move that one action up a level. That decision should be yours, never the agent’s.

    Recent findings suggest that for every action, record who asked for it, who approved it, what happened and when. It sounds bureaucratic, but it is the only way to answer when a customer, an auditor or your board asks, “Why did this happen?” Without a log, you also cannot tell when it is safe to give the agent more freedom.

    According to recent reports, none of this is about artificial intelligence. It is about making knowledge that lives in people’s heads, and in systems that do not talk to each other, available and trustworthy. Companies that do this get more out of their AI. They also become less fragile when a key person goes on holiday or leaves.

    Recent findings suggest that so start small. Book the two hours this week, write down 10 rules and test one link.

    #27820. Breaking: Trust Is The Fresh Battleground For Customer Engagement

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (931 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Trust Is The Fresh Battleground For Customer Engagement

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (931 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.
    • In a recent development, ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult.
    • Every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.

    In a recent development, ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult. Amid the meteoric rise of AI-enabled scams, call spoofing and social engineering attacks, the challenges organizations face when trying to reach consumers seem insurmountable.

    Every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage. Many of the traditional warning signs consumers were trained to recognize have disappeared—consumers are on edge.

    And with good reason: It’s a jungle out there.

    In our recent global study, “61% of business leaders ranked fraud among the risks with the greatest potential business impact, ahead of cybersecurity breaches, compliance, customer churn, operational cost and reputational risk. More concerning, 58% said they’re very or extremely concerned fraud is evolving faster than their organizations’ abilities to detect and prevent it.”.

    According to recent reports, historically, organizations have viewed fraud and engaging with customers as separate disciplines. But today’s threat environment makes it clear they’re deeply interconnected. In many cases, the communication channel itself—whether a phone call, text message, email or mobile app interaction—provides the first indication that fraud may be occurring.

    Sources indicate that consumers don’t experience fraud, identity and communication challenges as separate complications. To them, it’s one experience, one problem. It’s a trust problem that’s reshaping the customer journey. In fact, 69% of consumers say they would switch vendors for stronger security.

    Trust has become the foundation for both customer engagement and fraud prevention.

    Recent findings suggest that at our recent Fraud & Communications Summit in Chicago, keynote speaker Matt O’Neill, a former U.S. Secret Service Special Agent and recipient of Gold and Silver Awards for distinguished service, shared insights from years spent working undercover as a banker, broker, money launderer and other personas. In these roles, he led multinational investigations into crypto-laundering networks and dark web marketplaces.

    In a recent development, according to O’Neill, fraudsters are winning because fraud has evolved into a highly organized industry. He explained that scam operations now function much like large multinational corporations. Scam compounds are similar to call centers, complete with organizational structures, performance quotas, shift schedules and human resources departments. Unfortunately, many of these compounds operate under sophisticated criminal networks and employ workers who have been trafficked.

    According to recent reports, at the same time, the barrier to entry into the fraud world has never been lower. AI enables fraudsters to create convincing scams at scale in virtually any language, including cloned voices, deepfake videos and personalized social engineering campaigns. And it’s cheap.​.

    The consequences of eroding trust extend well beyond fraud losses. Organizations often experience:.

    • Reduced marketing effectiveness.

    Ironically, the industries and brands most trusted by consumers are frequently among the most targeted by fraudsters, with the highest fraud instances related to auto lending, bank-issued and retail credit cards and unsecured personal lending.

    According to Edelman, trust now rivals price and quality as a primary factor influencing consumer decision-making. Research indicates that “77% of consumers cited confidence their personal data is secure as the most important feature when choosing whom to transact with online.”.

    Organizations can strengthen trust by approaching fraud prevention and customer communications as a unified strategy.

    Traditional fraud controls were designed for predictable attacks. Today’s fraudsters adapt rapidly, vary their tactics and coordinate attacks across multiple channels and sessions. Identity verification remains important, but it only confirms who someone claims to be. It doesn’t determine whether the current interaction should be trusted.

    Here’s where identity verification falls short:.

    • KYC (Know Your Customer) controls are often strongest at onboarding, not throughout the customer lifecycle.

    • Devices, behaviors and risk profiles change over time.

    • Credentials can be compromised after verification.

    • Synthetic identities can appear legitimate on paper.

    The most important fraud signal is often not a single event. Any single signal can be manipulated or generate false positives. It’s the story that unfolds throughout an interaction. It emerges through relationships among users, devices, accounts, entities and sessions.

    According to recent reports, as if it wasn’t hard enough, AI has turbocharged fraud. In addition, labeling identified threats as AI-driven remains a challenge. That’s because it’s difficult to build comprehensive strategies with new AI fraud models evolving so rapidly.

    Industry observers note that while fraud practitioners know when an account was taken over, there’s currently no label for how it was taken over and whether AI drove the attack. As a result, the AI-attributed training set doesn’t exist yet for tracking that fraud, and detection stays anchored to heuristics and analyst judgment.

    To be able to engage effectively with consumers and prevent fraud, organizations must adopt continuous authentication and layered risk strategies.

    • Develop a comprehensive strategy—don’t address fraud in silos across your organization.

    • Form strategic partnerships with your cyber teams.

    • Correlate identity, device, behavioral and contextual signals in real time.

    Industry observers note that the process is straightforward: Collect. Correlate. Score. Decide.

    Every phone call, text message, email and digital transaction represents a trust moment. Customers want confidence the organization contacting them is legitimate and their information and transactions are protected. Simply asking consumers to “trust us” is no longer enough.

    Verified identity, authenticated communications and real-time risk intelligence are becoming the foundation of trust in a digital-first world.

    It has been revealed that the future isn’t reactive fraud mitigation. It’s proactive trust at the point of interaction, by orchestrating identity, risk and communications intelligence across every customer interaction.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    Cryptocurrency markets suffered another brutal sell-off on Friday, November 20, as a wave of selling across Wall Street spilled into digital assets. Bitcoin broke below the psychologically vital $60,000 level, while Ethereum and Solana experienced even steeper declines as investors continued to retreat from riskier assets.

    Industry observers note that as of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -5.66%) had plunged 6.01% to $58,186.39, while Ethereum (ETH -7.99%) tumbled 9.03% to $1,596.72 and Solana (SOL -5.97%) declined 8.02% to $67.21.     Sources indicate that deteriorating investor risk appetite continued to weigh on cryptocurrencies Friday as concerns over interest rates, elevated valuations, and tighter financial conditions fueled a broad sell-off across global markets. With the Nasdaq plunging more than 5%, investors appeared increasingly focused on raising cash and reducing exposure to riskier assets.

    The simultaneous decline in stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests selling pressure is extending beyond individual markets. Rather than simply rotating capital between asset classes, investors appear to be reducing their overall risk exposure, leaving cryptocurrencies particularly vulnerable as liquidity conditions continue to deteriorate.

    According to recent reports, spot cryptocurrency ETFs suffered steep losses on Friday, mirroring the broader sell-off in digital assets. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT -5.87%) fell 5.87%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC -6.16%) declined 5.97%.     By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than NiSource ›.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, NiSource (NI -0.63%) raised its long-term financial guidance while expanding its capital investment commitments. The utility is blending standard regulated energy distribution with power contracts for giant technology facilities.

    Three things management said stand out.

    It has been revealed that niSource signed a 20-year agreement with Microsoft, marking its fifth data center power contract across three technology giants. The projects run through Genco, the tech giant's power generation segment, and lower electricity bills for retail customers of NIPSCO, its electric utility subsidiary.

    Executive Vice President Shawn Anderson detailed a new seven-year spending forecast that dedicates $32 billion to core regulated utilities and $8 billion to data center generation. Management expects this capital deployment to support compound annual adjusted earnings per share, or net income divided by outstanding stock, growth of 10% to 11%.

    It has been revealed that utilities usually wait years to collect revenues on new construction, creating regulatory lag that drags on cash flows. NiSource uses forward-looking rate structures and tracker mechanisms, which are regulatory processes that let utilities recover specific investment costs quickly, to streamline cash generation.

    Sources indicate that large technology companies are expanding heavily across Northern Indiana, where available land, water access, and fiber networks give NiSource an operational edge over surrounding power grids. Management is watching regulatory approval schedules and construction milestones to ensure projects open on time.

    According to recent reports, the utility couples steady 6% to 8% earnings growth from its base gas and electric utilities with higher-margin growth from data center power contracts. That combination creates two complementary income streams that insulate shareholders from regulatory shifts in any single state.

    #27808. SpaceX Plans to Spend $2.8 Billion on Gas Turbines. Here’s What That Much Natural Gas Demand Means for Pipeline Investors.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (764 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    SpaceX Plans to Spend $2.8 Billion on Gas Turbines. Here’s What That Much Natural Gas Demand Means for Pipeline Investors.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus.
    • Industry observers note that that massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market.
    • Industry observers note that an easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:55PM EST.

    When SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus. SpaceX is purchasing those turbines to power its own data centers and factories.

    Industry observers note that that massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market. U.S. data centers already generate over 40% of their electricity from natural gas, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). That percentage could continue to rise as the cloud and AI markets expand.

    Industry observers note that an easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers. Pipeline operators charge companies "tolls" to use their infrastructure, so they're well-insulated from volatile commodity prices. Instead, they simply need the resources to keep flowing through their pipes to generate stable profits. Most pipeline companies also return lots of cash to their investors through high dividends and distributions.

    As demand for natural gas rises, pipeline companies will need to expand their infrastructure to handle the increased volumes. Those investments could compress their near-term margins, but they'll support their long-term growth. Let's see which of these pipeline operators will benefit the most from the rapid growth of the cloud infrastructure and AI data center markets.

    Recent findings suggest that the Williams Companies (WMB -2.75%) operates more than 32,000 miles of pipeline across 24 states. It owns Transco, the largest natural gas pipeline in the U.S., which connects the Gulf Coast to the Atlantic seaboard. Its pipelines handle roughly a third of all natural gas produced in the United States.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that unlike more diversified pipeline companies, Williams generates most of its revenue by gathering, processing, storing, and transporting natural gas. A smaller percentage of revenue comes from natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil handling services, and electricity generation.

    In a recent development, from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Williams' EPS to grow at a 12% CAGR. It still looks reasonably valued at 26 times next year's earnings, and it could command an even higher valuation if the data center market heats up again.

    Williams has raised its dividend annually over the past nine years, and it's paid continuous dividends for the past 52 years. It right now pays a forward yield of 3.2%, and its low payout ratio of 82% gives it ample room for future dividend hikes.

    Energy Transfer (ET +1.84%) operates more than 140,000 miles of pipeline across 44 states. It transports crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), and other refined products through its pipelines. It also exports NGLs through its marine export terminals.

    TXSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/02/26.

    Recent findings suggest that energy Transfer's pipelines transport about 30% of the natural gas produced in the United States. It generates only approximately 40% of its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) from natural gas, which makes it less of a direct play on natural gas than Williams. Still, Energy Transfer is more exposed to that market than many of its peers.

    According to recent reports, unlike Williams, which operates as a traditional corporation, Energy Transfer is a master limited partnership (MLP) that treats its investors as partners rather than shareholders. MLPs pay distributions -- much of which are classified as a "return of capital" for more tax-efficient returns -- rather than traditional dividends. That strategy enables it to pay a high forward yield of 7.2%, but its investors must file an additional K-1 form (for MLPs) with their taxes each year.

    According to recent reports, from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Energy Transfer's earnings per unit (EPU) to grow at a 13% CAGR. It trades at just 12 times next's year's EPU, and that low valuation should limit its downside even if the cloud and AI markets cool off over the next few years.

    Credo Technology Group vs. Western Digital: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:57PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Credo Technology Group ›.
    • Industry observers note that the race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Credo Technology Group ›.

    Industry observers note that the race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage. You might be deciding between Credo Technology Group (CRDO -15.20%) and Western Digital (WDC -12.02%) for 2027.

    It has been revealed that credo provides high-speed connectivity solutions that enable artificial intelligence data centers to communicate efficiently, while Western Digital is a global leader in both hard disk and flash storage. While they operate in different niches, both are essential players in the scaling of cloud infrastructure. This comparison evaluates which stock offers the best path for long-term growth.

    Industry observers note that credo Technology Group specializes in high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions designed for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company sells products like Active Electrical Cables and optical components to hyperscale operators and system vendors. It has established key partnerships with Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) and Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) to enhance connectivity for dual-architecture systems.

    In a recent development, the demand for faster semiconductor stocks has significantly boosted its financial performance. In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.6 billion, representing a 165.1% increase over the previous period. This expansion led to a net income of roughly $538.3 million and a net margin of about 33.8%.

    It has been revealed that as of its May 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, meaning the organization carries no debt relative to shareholder equity. Its current ratio is approximately 10.2x, indicating a strong ability to cover short-term debts with current assets. In the fiscal year ended May 2, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $407.0 million, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 39.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Sources indicate that western Digital designs and supplies essential data-storage solutions for enterprises and hyperscale cloud providers. Its product portfolio includes both hard disk drives and flash-based storage serving a global market across Asia and the Americas. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, with three individual clients accounting for 16%, 15%, and 13% of total net revenue in its latest annual report.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $14.5 billion, representing a 43% increase compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was nearly $10.0 billion, which indicates a net margin of roughly 69.2%. This performance suggests a robust recovery in cloud storage demand, which now accounts for nearly 89% of its net revenue.

    According to recent reports, on its July 2026 balance sheet, the tech giant reveals a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.1x, meaning total debt is low relative to equity. The current ratio stands at approximately 1.3x, measuring how well the company meets its short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended July 3, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $3.5 billion, representing operating cash flow minus capital expenditures.

    In a recent development, credo Technology Group faces intense competition from larger industry peers like Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%), Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%), and Astera Labs (ALAB -14.77%). The tech giant also deals with geopolitical risks due to its reliance on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for all semiconductor manufacturing. Furthermore, it manages previously flagged intellectual property litigation with Marvell Technology, which was recently resolved via a settlement.

    According to recent reports, western Digital must navigate risks associated with its complex strategic initiatives, such as the 2025 separation of its former flash business unit. It competes directly with other storage manufacturers like Seagate Technology Holdings (STX -12.35%) and providers of alternative storage technologies. Additionally, the organization relies on a limited supply base for critical components, leaving it exposed to potential global supply chain disruptions.

    Western Digital is cheaper, trading at a lower Forward P/E for future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio based on sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    It has been revealed that I'd go with Credo Technology, a firm whose sales have more than doubled year over year for seven straight quarters. AI data centers run on thousands of chips that need to share data quickly, and Credo is a key player that makes the connections between them.

    Industry observers note that management expects sales to grow more than 85% this fiscal year, and Credo is also very profitable, turning about half of its sales into adjusted profit. It's also moving into optical products that carry data farther than its copper cables can, and management expects them to bring in more than $600 million this fiscal year. The stock fell after its recent earnings report, as investors worried that a few massive customers make up most of its sales, but Credo added another big customer in its latest quarter.

    To its credit, Western Digital's hard drives store much of the data AI creates, and its profit has jumped. But rival Toshiba is reportedly doubling its hard drive capacity, which could pull prices down. For long-term investors, Credo pairs fast growth with strong profits, and it has a front-row seat as AI data centers get bigger. With plenty of cash on hand, it can keep investing in upcoming products for years to come.

    #27799. When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1320 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1320 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test newly introduced solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout.
    • In a recent development, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question.
    • In a recent development, A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test newly introduced solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout. But not every pilot warrants further investment, and knowing when to end one can be just as important as knowing when to expand it.

    In a recent development, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council share warning signs that indicate it’s time to end a technology pilot rather than extend it, redesign it or move it into production.

    In a recent development, A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot. Defining boundaries and expectations, and, importantly, being transparent, are critical to a pilot’s success. Owners should also share any uncertainty during the pilot instead of waiting for it to pivot or improve. - Arunava Sen, Tata Communications America Inc.

    A clear sign is when the pilot team cannot tell you what the technology accessed, what decisions it made, or what data it touched. If you cannot answer those questions in a controlled environment (test group), you will not answer them in production. - Michael Nicosia, Salt Security.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    It has been revealed that one sign a technology pilot shouldn’t progress doesn’t involve the upcoming tech itself but the tools teams already work with. If teams are working in siloed workflows with tools that don’t collaborate with one another, introducing new technology can drive up costs, increase complexity and hurt productivity. Connected tools and workflows are integral to the success of any new tech deployment. - Usman Shuja, Bluebeam.

    In a recent development, end a pilot when its success depends on hand-curated data that won’t exist in production. If someone cleaned the dataset, resolved definitions and fixed edge cases for the pilot, and no one owns doing that at scale in production, extending or redesigning the product in production won’t help. In many cases, technology isn’t the problem; the foundation is. Ask not whether the pilot worked, but what it worked on. - Prakash Reddy, Okta.

    In a recent development, if the pilot only works while its champion is in the room or while the vendor quietly does manual work behind the scenes, you’ve tested enthusiasm, not technology. Hand it to a team that didn’t build it for 30 days. If results collapse, you’d be pushing a dependency into production, not a tool. End it and keep the learnings. - Damian Wasserman, BEON.tech.

    Sources indicate that when the team stops asking what we learned and starts asking when we get to stop, that’s the sign. A pilot without defined success criteria is avoidance. If you can’t name the specific business result it was supposed to prove or disprove, extending it won’t help. End it, define the outcome you actually need, and redesign around that from the start. - Ali Alkhafaji, APPLY.

    Industry observers note that organizations should end a technology pilot when they have full visibility of the tool’s usage and cost metrics but still cannot connect either to a meaningful business outcome. Adoption alone is not enough without a clear path to measurable value, and extending the pilot risks turning experimentation into ongoing spend without a business case. - Conal Gallagher, Flexera.

    Recent findings suggest that A clear sign is when the people who were supposed to benefit stop asking about it. Pilots drag on because the sponsors like the idea, not because users need it. If the pilot group has quietly gone back to their old way of working and nobody complains when the tool goes down, there’s nothing to extend. Name the lesson, thank the team and end it. - Hastimal Jangid, Coozmoo Digital Solutions, Inc.

    A pilot should be reconsidered when it performs well in a demo but can’t prove that it solves a real business problem. AI makes it easy to add capabilities, but more features don’t always mean more value. Teams need clear measures of success and feedback loops to understand what’s working and what’s not before investing further. - Tony Grout, M-Files.

    A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when it repeatedly fails to demonstrate measurable business value despite validated assumptions and reasonable adjustments. If the solution cannot deliver meaningful ROI, operational efficiency or strategic impact, extending it only increases sunk costs. Strong leadership means knowing when to stop, not just when to scale. - Kameshwar Singh, Cohesity.

    According to recent reports, end a pilot if no effort was spent defining the vision and how value will be realized at scale. That’s like building a bridge from both ends without deciding where it should meet. - Venky Ramesh, LatentView Analytics.

    A pilot should end when success depends on conditions that production will never have: handpicked data, expert users, manual fixes, privileged integrations or constant vendor support. If removing that scaffolding collapses the value case, extending the pilot only perfects the illusion. The real test is not, “Does it work?” but, “Does it still create measurable value when exposed to ordinary users, messy data, real constraints and an ordinary day?” - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

    End a pilot when making the technology operable, reliable and governable outweighs its business value. If protecting sensitive data, maintaining an audit trail and providing human oversight would cost more than the expected benefit, extending that particular pilot needs a stronger business case than the time and money already invested. - Brian Stimpfl, S-Docs.

    According to recent reports, end a pilot when the evidence invalidates its core business premise. If people can complete the workflow but gain no meaningful time, cost or quality improvement over the current process, more engineering won’t create demand. Define that minimum benefit before launch, test it with real users, and stop when it remains out of reach. - Irina Shymko, Langate Software.

    End the pilot when the team cannot define a credible path from the experiment to a measurable business outcome. If success still depends on vague future improvements, heroic manual support or assumptions the pilot was supposed to validate, extending it usually just delays the decision. - Dhyey Mavani, Abridge.

    It has been revealed that A pilot should end when the team cannot explain what newly introduced evidence another extension will produce. Every extra week should answer a specific open question about value, risk, adoption, cost or scale. Once the remaining time is only keeping the pilot alive, the experiment has already delivered its answer. - Sibasis Padhi, Walmart Inc.

    I would end a pilot when it successfully completes individual tasks but repeatedly fails to deliver the full business outcome. Often, the underlying concern is the absence of a clear decision model for handling exceptions, approvals or unresolved work across teams. If nobody can authorize what happens next, scaling the technology only scales the problem. - Vamshi Noothi, Cisco.

    It has been revealed that A pilot should be ended if nobody uses it unless someone reminds them. A pilot that only stays alive while its sponsor keeps pushing won’t survive production, and extending it just postpones that answer. Software nobody uses isn’t free; it still costs money to run, maintain and support. End it, write down what you learned about the problem, and put the team on something people actually want. - Jeremy Suriel, Kustomer.

    A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when no business owner is willing to take responsibility for implementation. Even if the technology performs well, success requires business ownership, accountability and commitment to change. Without a sponsor willing to champion the solution, allocate resources and own the outcomes, extending the pilot is unlikely to deliver value. Technology cannot create lasting benefits without clear business ownership. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Is Coca-Cola a Millionaire-Maker Stock?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%).
    • Over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame.
    • It has been revealed that to understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Ebiefung – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    Few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%). Since its founding in the late 19th century, the multinational beverage maker has expanded globally to serve billions and become one of the world's most recognized brands. Investors have profited substantially along the way, and this shows little sign of stopping.

    Over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame. This is a major deal for a organization that is already large and mature. Let's dig deeper into the pros and cons of Coca-Cola to decide if the company still has millionaire-maker potential.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that to understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett. His Berkshire Hathaway portfolio owns a whopping $38.4 billion worth of Coca-Cola stock, making it his third-largest bet behind American Express and Apple.

    Buffett likes to invest in companies with simple and easy-to-understand business models that enjoy a strong economic moat. A moat is a competitive advantage that protects a company's market share against competition and allows it to enjoy stable or elevated pricing power. Coca-Cola is arguably the quintessential example of this type of business.

    You can walk into a convenience store or restaurant practically anywhere in the world and find Coca-Cola's flagship beverage Coke (or one of its many subbrands like Sprite, Fanta, and a variety of localized options).

    The company's ubiquitous shelf space has created unparalleled habit creation among its consumers, which is something fresh rivals will struggle to disrupt, even if they manage to create better-tasting products. This advantage also makes Coca-Cola's sales remarkably recession-resistant. It has allowed the company to protect its margins amid soaring global inflation in raw materials like aluminum and sugar.

    In a recent development, coca-Cola's gross margins have hovered around 60%, despite the soaring prices for its products. This suggests the manufacturer is passing on the vast majority of inflation to consumers, while protecting its own profitability.

    KO Gross Profit Margin data by YCharts.

    It has been revealed that coca-Cola isn't without some long-term challenges. The company is already a global brand name, and that means there is very little room for organic growth. Management will be increasingly tempted to rely on price increases to juice investor returns. While the company's gross margin of over 60% was easy to justify back when a 12-pack cost $4.00, it is much harder to stomach when prices have doubled, and more American families are struggling to make ends meet.

    It has been revealed that soda prices have far exceeded the U.S. inflation rate, despite boasting a disproportionately middle- and lower-income consumer base. It's hard not to wonder if this situation is as sustainable as it may look on the surface.

    Over the long term, there could be a generational shift away from brand-name soft drinks as people become more comfortable buying lower-cost store brands from major retailers like Walmart, which offers alternatives like Sam's Cola and Twist Up.

    It has been revealed that coca-Cola's recent performance is impressive, and its strong moat can help set the company up for more market-beating growth over the long term. That stated, with a market cap of $422 billion (in a mature industry with relatively little room for organic growth), Coca-Cola's days of explosive millionaire-making growth are likely behind it. Shares are also somewhat expensive at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 28.

    Investors who buy the stock now should look at it as a safer alternative to more speculative opportunities like generative AI. The company's dividend (right now boasting a yield of 2.21%) will likely represent a sizable percentage of its long-term returns.

    In a recent development, when our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 768%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 199% for the S&P 500.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (715 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Pfizer's Launched and Acquired Drugs Grew 32% in Q3 — and 3 Other Reasons to Buy the Stock Before 2027

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.
    • Recent findings suggest that pfizer (PFE -0.51%) faces a large patent cliff, and investors worry it won't be able to offset the revenue it loses as older drugs face generic competition.
    • Industry observers note that in fact, revenue from recently launched and acquired drugs rose 32% in the third quarter of 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Pfizer ›.

    Recent findings suggest that pfizer (PFE -0.51%) faces a large patent cliff, and investors worry it won't be able to offset the revenue it loses as older drugs face generic competition. That's a problem, but the drugmaker is aware of it and is making important strides in its efforts to address the concern. The big story, however, is that this issue is pretty normal for a drug firm.

    Industry observers note that in fact, revenue from recently launched and acquired drugs rose 32% in the third quarter of 2026. That shows the pharmaceutical giant's efforts are bearing fruit. But there's more reason to be excited, including the firm's strong balance sheet, its large dividend, and management's commitment to continue paying that dividend. Here's what you need to know.

    One of the biggest worries about Pfizer is its upcoming patent expirations. Two big ones are Eliquis in 2028 and Vyndamax in 2031. But patent expirations are a normal part of the pharma sector. And research and development efforts in the highly technical and intensely competitive healthcare sector don't always align perfectly with a tech giant's patent expiration schedule. It's just a fact of life.

    The 32% revenue growth Pfizer achieved from introduced and acquired products is evidence that the organization is seeing some success in its efforts to address the matter. And it sets up three more reasons to consider buying the stock.

    It has been revealed that pfizer ended the third quarter of 2026 with $1.8 billion in cash and $12.4 billion in short-term investments. That gives the tech giant significant firepower to support its business through this patent-expiration cycle. In fact, the company's cash hoard is slightly higher than at the start of the year, so it isn't rapidly burning through its savings.

    Despite the organization's results with newly introduced drugs and its financial strength, investors are deeply negative on Pfizer's stock. That's highlighted by its huge 6.1% dividend yield as of this writing. To put that yield into context, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) yields roughly 1.1%, and the average pharma stock yields 1.3%.

    The negativity highlighted by the elevated yield is echoed by more traditional valuation metrics. Pfizer's price-to-sales and price-to-book ratios are below their five-year averages. And while the price-to-earnings ratio is elevated, it is largely due to one-time charges. Looking at the whole picture, Pfizer's stock looks attractively priced.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Given the lofty yield, Pfizer is likely to be most appealing to dividend-focused investors. But right now earnings aren't covering the dividend. That's not a great sign, but one-time charges are part of the problem. If you look at cash flow, the tech giant can still support the dividend. That's highlighted by a cash dividend payout ratio of roughly 85%. While a lower number would be better, there's still some room for adversity. And don't forget about the company's large cash pile.

    Both of these facts help support management's strong backing of the dividend. Indeed, one of Pfizer's key capital priorities is to "maintain and grow our dividend." Obviously, the company's priorities could change, but it wouldn't make a statement like that if the board of directors wasn't on board with protecting the dividend.

    In a recent development, at the end of the day, Pfizer is facing very real headwinds today. But it is an industry-leading tech giant with a long history of success. If history is any guide, it will muddle through this difficult period. The success it is having with latest drugs, its financial strength, attractive valuation, and dedication to its large dividend are all strong reasons for investors to take a deep dive before 2026 is over. If you wait too long, the opportunity here may pass you by.

    BigBear.ai vs. Innodata: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:29PM EST.
    • Choosing between these specialized AI plays requires balancing high-stakes government work against commercial data engineering growth.
    • BigBear.ai provides complex decision intelligence tools for federal and defense agencies, while Innodata helps major tech firms train generative AI systems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:29PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than BigBear.ai ›.

    Choosing between these specialized AI plays requires balancing high-stakes government work against commercial data engineering growth. Investors must decide if BigBear.ai (BBAI -8.67%) or Innodata (INOD -8.91%) better suits their portfolio needs.

    BigBear.ai provides complex decision intelligence tools for federal and defense agencies, while Innodata helps major tech firms train generative AI systems. Both companies operate in the rapidly evolving world of artificial intelligence but serve different markets. This comparison examines their financial health, customer concentration, and valuation to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.

    According to recent reports, bigBear.ai offers decision intelligence solutions that combine data from different sources to help leaders make faster choices. It serves critical sectors like national security, cybersecurity, and global supply chains. According to its latest annual report, a specific contract accounted for nearly 51% of consolidated revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

    Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $142.1 million. This represented a revenue growth decline of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior period. The company reported a net loss of roughly $180.2 million during this same time frame.

    Recent findings suggest that following its early 2026 debt conversion, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.0x, meaning the company carries virtually no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 1.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was negative at nearly $46.3 million.

    Innodata operates as a global data engineering firm that prepares and evaluates data for large-scale AI systems. The manufacturer serves several high-profile technology leaders, with one customer in its digital data solutions segment accounting for nearly 58% of total revenue in 2025. This focus on the best small cap tech stocks in the data sector highlights its role in the generative AI boom.

    Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $350.2 million. This reflects a revenue growth increase of nearly 46.9% over the previous year. The firm also achieved a net income of roughly $48.5 million during this period.

    In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 2.7x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating a strong balance sheet with no total debt. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $35.6 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    BigBear.ai faces significant risk due to heavy revenue concentration with government customers who can terminate contracts for convenience. Scaling its sales efforts remains a challenge while managing long and unpredictable sales cycles. It also faces intense competition from Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). The organization also navigates complex AI deployment risks and recent financial volatility including litigation over accounting errors.

    Innodata relies heavily on a single customer that contributed nearly 58% of its 2025 revenues, making it vulnerable to contract changes. It competes against well-resourced firms like Accenture (ACN +1.19%) and Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH +3.11%) in the data engineering space. The business also deals with geopolitical risks from its global workforce and ongoing legal challenges regarding securities class actions.

    Innodata appears to offer a more attractive value proposition based on its lower P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Innodata. AI models are only as good as the data they learn from, and Innodata helps massive tech companies create and test that data. Its sales have grown year over year for 13 straight quarters, and it makes money.

    Last quarter, sales jumped 53% and management raised its growth outlook, though the stock has fallen sharply this fall. There are risks: Two customers make up most of its sales, margins narrowed, and one program is winding down. But Innodata is adding newly introduced customers and work from a large cloud organization, and expects to replace the lost program by early next year.

    It has been revealed that to give BigBear.ai its due, it does high-stakes work for national security and border security customers with contracts that are difficult to replace, and its backlog is growing. But it's still losing money, and government contract sales can be difficult to predict. That uncertainty is where Innodata stands apart: It is already profitable, with plenty of cash to keep investing as demand for AI data grows.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Healy – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Amazon (AMZN -4.10%), a global e-commerce, cloud, and digital advertising platform, closed at $246.82, down 4.10%. Shares fell on Friday amid an AI and mega-cap tech sell-off, while investors are watching capital spending, margins, and AWS growth.Trading volume reached 72.1M shares, coming in about 79% above its three-month average of 40.2M shares. Amazon.com IPO'd in 1997 and has grown 251,971% since going public.

    Sources indicate that S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) closed at 6,910, down 3.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) finished at 22,617, down 5.28%. Among broadline retail and cloud computing peers, Walmart (WMT +1.51%) closed at $127.95, up 1.52%, while eBay (EBAY -1.39%) closed at $115.59, down 1.39%; Walmart's stronger holiday outlook highlighted steadier consumer demand than Amazon.com's pressure points.

    Negative sentiment from both its e-commerce and AWS segments seemed to weigh on Amazon stock today.

    Soft consumer spending and an increased need for promotional discounting led it to underperform retail counterparts like Walmart, which, as previously mentioned, rose in today's trading session.

    Moreover, capital expenditures (capex) continue to weigh on the stock. The company's initiative to spend $220 billion has led to free cash outflows, a concerning sign for a company that generated tens of billions in annual free cash flow until recently. Furthermore, despite a massive amount of liquidity, it has had to turn to the debt markets in a rising-rate environment.

    Sources indicate that such concerns were not unique to Amazon, and every stock in the Magnificent Seven, which contend with many of the same challenges, dropped today. Additionally, the Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) IPO has put AI in the spotlight this week. That stock has trended down since opening at $111.50 per share yesterday, likely adding to the negative sentiment surrounding AI.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Admittedly, at a P/E ratio of 20, Amazon stock looks like an increasingly attractive buy, arguably making it the one hyperscaler through 2030 that investors should buy and hold. Nonetheless, with Amazon stock caught in the current downturn, investors should probably move cautiously if they choose to invest.
