    • Industry observers note that globant (GLOB +4.13%) was one of the rare stocks to rise amid the sharp decline of the wider market on Friday.
    • Globant's third-quarter revenue was $611.1 million, down 1% year over year.
    • That earnings per share (EPS) figure met analyst expectations while revenue notched a slight beat.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Eric Volkman – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:48PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Globant ›.

    Industry observers note that globant (GLOB +4.13%) was one of the rare stocks to rise amid the sharp decline of the wider market on Friday. It acquired that port-in-a-storm quality on its latest set of quarterly results, which were good enough to draw investors to its equity. The digital transformation specialist's shares ended the day more than 4% higher.

    Globant's third-quarter revenue was $611.1 million, down 1% year over year. Non-IFRS (adjusted) net income also declined, falling by almost 9% to nearly $63.8 million, or $1.48 per share.

    That earnings per share (EPS) figure met analyst expectations while revenue notched a slight beat. The pundit top-line consensus for that line item was $610.9 million.

    Recent findings suggest that like the more progressive legacy software companies, Globant -- which specializes in developing custom software for enterprises automating aspects of their business -- has embraced artificial intelligence (AI) in its solutions. It said in its earnings release that its recently introduced AI Pods subscription service had doubled its annualized run rate.

    Globant quoted co-founder and CEO Martin Migoya as saying that "We are seeing growing enterprise adoption as clients shift from hourly billing toward outcome- and consumption-based delivery.".

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It's one thing to embrace AI as either a tool for internal software development or to tack on some of its functionalities to an existing software suite. It's quite another to lead with it as a product offering, like Globant is doing with AI Pods.

    Sources indicate that the service is clearly resonating with the market, and I think it might soon become a driver of growth for this company given its relatively high margins. This is starting to look something like a sleeper stock among the many software titles on the market, and as such, it's well worth watching.

    #27757. Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 67

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (655 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 67

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.
    • According to recent reports, the average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025.
    • Reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.

    According to recent reports, the average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later. It's the point where you're eligible for your unreduced retirement amount.

    Reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount. Many people who are 67 today have a full retirement age of 66 years and 10 months. These workers may have already earned small delayed retirement credits if they waited until 67 to claim their checks.

    Earnings histories also impact these averages. Men who are 67 receive an average of $2,234.41 per month, while the average among women is $1,801.82. This results in a monthly gender gap of $432.59 as of December 2025.

    Think of your full retirement age as the baseline for your benefits. The SSA bases your check on your average monthly income over your 35 highest-earning years, adjusting those wages for inflation and applying the primary insurance amount formula. This calculation creates the standard amount you're entitled to at full retirement age.

    Sources indicate that you don't have to claim at your baseline. You can earn delayed retirement credits, which are increases for delaying past FRA, worth 8% per year up to age 70. For a worker whose FRA is 67, waiting those three extra years provides a 24% total increase in monthly income.

    According to recent reports, these decisions have a visible impact on the data. The average monthly benefit at age 70 is $2,274.68, which is $258.20 higher than the age-67 average.

    But even for these claimants, benefits alone often aren't enough to live on. Social Security was only designed to replace about 40% of pre-retirement wages, so most retirees rely on savings or other income to cover their full costs.

    In a recent development, A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027 to help benefits keep pace with inflation. This will add about $73 a month on top of the average listed above. These adjustments are designed to protect your purchasing power over time.

    Knowing the population average gives you a target for your own planning, but your final check depends on your career earnings and when you choose to claim.

    Waiting until age 67 to claim Social Security helps you avoid the early claiming benefit reduction, which can drastically reduce your checks. This is one major reason FRA is such a popular claiming age, but it's not the only one.

    Sources indicate that when you claim Social Security under your FRA, you're also at risk of losing some of your benefits to the earnings test if you're still working. In 2027, for example, you lose $1 from your checks for every $2 you earn over $25,960 if you're under your FRA all year. If you'll reach your FRA next year, you only lose $1 for every $3 you earn over $67,920.

    Recent findings suggest that these lost benefits come back to you as a permanent benefit boost at your FRA. But for some, the risk of short-term losses makes them delay their claim until their FRA, when the earnings test no longer applies. This is something to weigh if you plan to continue working once you're eligible for Social Security checks.

    For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

    #27747. PayPal vs. SoFi Technologies: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (938 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    PayPal vs. SoFi Technologies: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.
    • Deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth.
    • In a recent development, payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than PayPal ›.

    Deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth. Both companies are fighting for a larger share of your digital wallet today.

    In a recent development, payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic. While they operate in different niches, both compete for the same pool of consumer financial activity, making them frequent candidates for a fintech-focused portfolio as investors look toward the future of money.

    It has been revealed that payPal operates a massive digital payments platform serving nearly 439 million active accounts across 200 markets. It provides branded checkout services, person-to-person payments via Venmo, and even Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) trading within its app. This scale makes it one of the most recognizable names in fintech stocks today as it adapts to a changing financial landscape.

    Industry observers note that reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each firm's latest full fiscal year. For FY 2025, PayPal reported revenue of nearly $33.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 4.3% over the prior year. The company generated net income of close to $5.2 billion, showing a steady ability to convert its high volume of transactions into profit for its shareholders.

    In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached roughly 0.5x, comparing total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was approximately 1.3x. Free cash flow, or the cash remaining after paying for operations and equipment, was nearly $5.6 billion in FY 2025.

    In a recent development, soFi Technologies is a mobile-first financial services provider that offers a wide range of products including student loan refinancing, home loans, and investment tools. It serves approximately 15.8 million members and has expanded into business services through a partnership with Mastercard (MA -0.14%). The organization also supports Bitcoin trading and provides modern banking infrastructure to other firms through its proprietary technology segments.

    For its latest annual report covering FY 2025, SoFi Technologies generated revenue of nearly $3.6 billion, which was an increase of approximately 35.1% compared to the previous year. The tech giant reported net income of close to $481.3 million, marking a significant transition into consistent profitability. This growth was driven by a diversified mix of lending products and financial services that attracted latest members to its platform.

    Based on its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.2x, helping investors see the low level of debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 0.2x, which measures a manufacturer's ability to cover immediate liabilities with assets that can be quickly converted to cash. Free cash flow for the year was a net loss of nearly $4.0 billion, which often occurs in banking as capital is deployed into fresh loans rather than held as cash.

    PayPal faces intense competition from both traditional banks and newer technology platforms that offer digital checkout solutions. The company is also subject to extensive global regulatory oversight regarding payment processing and anti-money laundering rules. Any failure to manage cybersecurity risks or protect user data could lead to significant penalties and damage its reputation.

    SoFi Technologies must manage the complex regulatory requirements that come with being a bank holding manufacturer. It relies on a concentrated number of whole loan purchasers, meaning its results could suffer if these buyers reduce their activity. Additionally, the company faces the challenge of managing rapid growth across its various lending and technology segments without increasing credit risks.

    When comparing these two companies using Forward P/E, PayPal looks significantly cheaper than its peer based on future earnings estimates.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    It has been revealed that I'd go with SoFi Technologies. Its sales and earnings are both growing far faster than PayPal's, and it has built a full digital bank with more than 17 million members, starting from student loans. Its bank charter lets it fund loans with its members' deposits, a cost advantage most fintech rivals lack.

    According to recent reports, soFi also gave investors its 2027 outlook a full quarter early, and it came in above analysts' expectations, with revenue expected to grow about 27%. Management built it assuming interest rates keep rising, even after a rate hike this year hurt the stock. The shares are still down for the year, so long-term investors get a lower price for a profitable, growing business.

    To give PayPal its due, it is a household name that produces plenty of cash, and Venmo is growing fast. But its original business, letting shoppers pay online with their PayPal account, is barely growing, and overall sales are rising slowly. By contrast, SoFi's lending and banking businesses are surging, and even its technology business, which lost a large client, is expected to return to growth in 2027. For long-term investors, that mix of growth, profits, and a lower price makes SoFi the better buy for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business.
    • In a recent development, except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't.
    • Industry observers note that rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business. A tech giant that's set to triple its top line over the course of the next couple of years, though? That seems outrageous.

    In a recent development, except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't. This future business is already lined up. These paying customers are just waiting for one pivotal milestone that's likely to materialize sometime next year. Then the floodgates open.

    Industry observers note that rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions. Its relatively small Electron rocket design has now been debuted 100 times, putting 273 satellites into low earth orbit.

    The organization also provides a range of satellite components and construction services, which accounts for more than half of last quarter's revenue of $268 million. Rocket Lab expects to do around $980 billion in business in fiscal 2026, well up from last year's $602 billion.

    This is just a taste of what's to come, though. As the organization announced with its third-quarter report posted earlier this month, Rocket Lab's backlog grew 52% from Q2's $2.36 billion to an incredible $3.6 billion. The organization just needs more capacity, but that's coming. Rocket Lab can now manufacture an Electron rocket every eight days.

    According to recent reports, then there's the proverbial 800-pound gorilla in the room. That's the tech giant's larger Neutron rocket, which has seen its inaugural flight pushed back several times, with the first flight now expected sometime in 2027.

    It has been revealed that despite the delays so far, once Neutron is flying, everything takes a turn for the better. As CFO Adam Spice commented during the third-quarter's earnings conference call, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) "will turn positive within six months of that first successful test flight," with cash flow likely to turn positive shortly after that.

    Recent findings suggest that neutron isn't the major profit center in and of itself, to be clear. It's just a means to an end. Being able to put larger, heavier satellites into orbit also opens up its satellite tech business. Of its newly introduced backlog of $3.6 billion, $1.7 billion of it reflects space systems rather than launch services, up 194% year over year.

    To this end, while analysts aren't yet looking for Rocket Lab's revenue to triple between now and 2028, with recent failures of similar rockets like ULA's Vulcan and one earlier in the year from Blue Origin, Rocket Lab is swiftly becoming a preferred launch option. It may well exceed 2028's expectations.

    As for the impact on the stock, it's not a complicated prediction to make. If the company's top line comes anywhere close to tripling by 2028, the bullish argument firms up enormously.

    Recent findings suggest that while it may not triple in value in step with revenue, $3 billion in sales could turn this high-growth $34 billion outfit into a $60 billion outfit with relative ease. And given that the company isn't likely to raise money by issuing more stock anytime soon, that translates into a near-doubling of the stock's price.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Tech Report: Prediction: Nvidia Stock Will Do This in the 6 Months After a New CEO Takes Over, According to History

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (901 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) is navigating one of the most consequential leadership transitions in recent Silicon Valley history.
    • Colette Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, is now serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
    • In a recent development, history offers some clues about how technology stocks behave following major CEO transitions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:42PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) is navigating one of the most consequential leadership transitions in recent Silicon Valley history. Following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid a controversy involving alleged connections to Chinese intelligence, investors are growing increasingly concerned about the organization's future. This uncertainty is weighing heavily on Nvidia stock, even as its underlying business continues to deliver extraordinary financial results.

    Colette Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, is now serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. According to reports, the organization is considering external candidates, including Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.

    In a recent development, history offers some clues about how technology stocks behave following major CEO transitions. However, Nvidia's circumstances are quite different from those of its peers, making the company's financial outlook particularly important right now.

    According to recent reports, microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) represents a successful example of a technology leadership transition. Satya Nadella became CEO on Feb. 4, 2014, replacing Steve Ballmer after Microsoft conducted a formal succession search. Nadella had previously led Microsoft's cloud and enterprise businesses, giving him extensive knowledge of the organization's operations.

    It has been revealed that microsoft stock advanced roughly 19% during Nadella's first six months as CEO. Of course, over the long term, he helped transform the Windows developer into a cloud computing powerhouse.

    Sources indicate that alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) offers another example. Sundar Pichai became CEO of Alphabet on Dec. 3, 2019, succeeding co-founder Larry Page. However, Pichai had already served as Google's CEO since 2015, making the transition more of a consolidation of leadership responsibilities than an unexpected management overhaul.

    Alphabet stock was higher roughly six months later, despite experiencing a meaningful drawdown during the short-lived COVID-19 market crash. Moreover, Page and his co-founder Sergey Brin remained involved as shareholders and directors, providing continuity that Nvidia currently lacks.

    Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) experienced a different outcome when Andy Jassy succeeded Jeff Bezos on July 5, 2021. Jassy was another internal executive who had previously built and led Amazon Web Services (AWS). Although Bezos relinquished the CEO position, he remains executive chairman, preserving his influence over the organization's long-term strategy.

    It has been revealed that amazon shares declined approximately 6% during Jassy's first six months as CEO. At the time, investors were assessing the impacts of slowing pandemic-era growth and rising operating expenses on Amazon's e-commerce marketplace.

    Recent findings suggest that the three examples above show that CEO succession can bring different short-term outcomes. However, they also share an key characteristic: Each of these companies promoted an experienced internal executive through an orderly transition, unlike Nvidia's abrupt leadership disruption.

    Nvidia's situation is unusual because Huang wasn't just another corporate executive. He co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent more than three decades directing the organization's evolution from a graphics chip manufacturer into the world's leading supplier of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. His influence extended across engineering, product development, corporate culture, and customer relationships.

    It has been revealed that as a result of his departure, investors are increasingly questioning whether Nvidia can maintain its technological edge without the executive who helped establish it. The uncertainty is compounded by growing competition from custom AI accelerators developed by Alphabet, Amazon, and other hyperscalers. Nvidia's next CEO needs to prove they can preserve the manufacturer's innovation-driven culture while navigating complicated supply chains and regulatory relationships.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Despite the unusual circumstances, Nvidia's financial outlook provides a compelling reason to anticipate a meaningful recovery. During its fiscal third-quarter earnings call, management increased its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75%, up from its previous outlook of 70%. This suggests demand for Nvidia's accelerated computing platforms remains strong despite Huang's departure.

    Recent findings suggest that furthermore, Nvidia expects to generate $130 billion in revenue during the fourth quarter -- representing 91% growth year over year. The company is also forecasting gross margins of between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028, suggesting that accelerating sales growth will translate into additional profits.

    Nvidia's share repurchase program provides another subtle catalyst for the stock. In September, the board increased the firm's existing authorization by $150 billion, leaving approximately $227.3 billion available at the end of the third quarter. Management intends to execute the remaining authorization by the end of fiscal 2028.

    Sources indicate that by reducing the number of outstanding shares, stock buybacks can increase earnings per share (EPS) even if net income is unchanged. Combined with Nvidia's revenue growth and profit margins, upcoming share repurchases should fuel substantial EPS expansion over the coming year.

    Sources indicate that my prediction is that Nvidia stock will trade higher six months after its new CEO assumes the role. The appointment itself should remove the primary source of uncertainty around the company, allowing investors to concentrate once again on revenue growth, earnings power, and competitive advantages.

    Here's How Much Nvidia Stock Is Worth Without Jensen Huang, According to Dan Ives

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has experienced a stunning reversal following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid controversy surrounding alleged connections to Chinese intelligence.
    • In a recent development, the magnitude of the decline is anything but trivial.
    • Nevertheless, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives thinks investors are overlooking Nvidia's underlying earnings power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:10PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has experienced a stunning reversal following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid controversy surrounding alleged connections to Chinese intelligence. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the semiconductor behemoth can maintain its technological edge without the executive who spent more than three decades building the company. Those concerns have contributed to a dramatic sell-off, even as Nvidia continues reporting ridiculously good financial results.

    In a recent development, the magnitude of the decline is anything but trivial. Nvidia stock reached a record closing price of around $239 in early October but has fallen to roughly $136 as of Nov. 20. That represents a decline of roughly 43%, wiping out more than $2.5 trillion in market capitalization and pushing Nvidia from the world's most valuable public tech giant to fourth place.

    NVDA Market Cap data by YCharts.

    Nevertheless, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives thinks investors are overlooking Nvidia's underlying earnings power. Although he acknowledges that Huang's departure changes the company's investment thesis, his revised price target suggests meaningful upside remains.

    Recent findings suggest that ives has been particularly vocal about the consequences of Huang's resignation. During a recent interview, he estimated that Huang contributed $1 trillion to Nvidia's valuation. In a separate appearance, Ives described Huang as the manufacturer's "heart and lungs," emphasizing his influence over Nvidia's technological roadmap and competitive position.

    Ives says Nvidia stock is worth $225 without Huang and $300 with him as CEO. These figures provide an interesting way to quantify the so-called Jensen premium. The difference between Ives' two valuations is $75 per share, representing a 25% reduction from his original $300 target.

    Recent findings suggest that the implied difference in market capitalization is actually considerably larger than the $1 trillion Ives alluded to. With approximately 24.2 billion shares outstanding, a $75 difference translates into roughly $1.8 trillion in equity value. At Ives' respective price targets, Nvidia would command a market capitalization of approximately $7.3 trillion with Huang and $5.4 trillion without him.

    The difference in valuation illustrates the enormous importance Wall Street places on Nvidia's founder and why investors have reacted so negatively to his departure.

    Dan Ives. Image source: Getty Images.

    Huang's value extends beyond his responsibilities as CEO. Since co-founding Nvidia in 1993, he has overseen the tech giant's transformation from a graphics processing company into the dominant supplier of accelerated computing infrastructure. His investments in GPUs, CUDA software, and AI computing helped position Nvidia at the center of the technology industry's most vital transformation since the birth of the internet.

    Perhaps Huang's greatest contribution has been leading Nvidia's culture of innovation. Huang consistently anticipated computing trends years before they became commercially relevant. This enabled Nvidia to develop new chip architectures and software ecosystems that competitors have struggled to replicate. This foresight helps establish durable competitive advantages and contributes to the organization's pricing power.

    Sources indicate that huang also cultivated relationships with other technology executives, hyperscalers, governments, and AI labs. These supply chain connections have become key as Nvidia participates in data center build-outs that require complex financing arrangements and long-term strategic commitments.

    Recent findings suggest that with all of that remarked, Nvidia's competitive advantages are not going to disappear just because Huang stepped away. The organization's hardware and software ecosystem, engineering workforce, customer relationships, and product roadmap remain intact.

    Moreover, Ives acknowledges that Nvidia has a lead of two to three years over its competitors in AI chip technology. Although Huang's departure could narrow that advantage over time, the company's existing leadership provides a robust foundation for future growth.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    Recent findings suggest that despite reducing his Nvidia price target from $300 to $225, Ives maintains a bullish outlook on the company. At approximately $136 per share, his revised target implies roughly 65% upside, while his original $300 estimate implies 121% potential appreciation.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Importantly, Ives' optimism centers on the insatiable demand for AI computing infrastructure and Nvidia's technological advantages. Following the tech giant's earnings report on Nov. 17, Ives wrote that the results answered a critical question: "Demand did not leave with him.".

    Recent findings suggest that the financial evidence supports that assessment. Nvidia generated $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, representing 103% growth year over year, while data center revenue surged 110% to $107.6 billion. The company also reported a gross margin of 74.8%, demonstrating that its pricing power remains strong.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Nvidia forecast $130 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%. This forecast suggests the company is poised for further expansion despite the leadership transition.

    According to recent reports, the central takeaway from Ives' analysis is that Nvidia doesn't necessarily need Huang to remain an attractive investment. Although his departure has reduced -- for now -- the premium investors are willing to pay, his price target still suggests considerable appreciation over the coming year. For investors who can stomach short-term volatility, Nvidia's recent sell-off could represent an opportunity to buy the dip in the most dominant AI infrastructure business at a significantly discounted valuation.

    #27727. Industry News: Bristol Myers Squibb's Growth Portfolio Just Hit $7.7 Billion. Is This Cheap Pharma Stock a No-Brainer Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (699 w)

    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Bristol Myers Squibb's Growth Portfolio Just Hit $7.7 Billion. Is This Cheap Pharma Stock a No-Brainer Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.
    • According to recent reports, bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +0.79%) is a large, well-respected pharmaceutical manufacturer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.

    According to recent reports, bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +0.79%) is a large, well-respected pharmaceutical manufacturer. It traces its history back to the mid-1800s. Right now, the company's portfolio of newer drugs, which it calls its "growth portfolio", just generated nearly $7.7 billion in revenue in a single quarter. That's a 12% increase over the same quarter in 2025. But is the stock worth buying? The risk/reward balance looks tilted toward reward for all but the most conservative investors. Here's why.

    The success Bristol Myers Squibb is having with its growth portfolio clearly indicates that this pharmaceutical giant hasn't lost its mojo. But investors are still downbeat on the stock (more on this below). So the dividend yield is a lofty 4.3%. The S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) yields roughly 1.1%, the average healthcare stock yields 1.3%, and the average drug stock yields 1.3%. That above-market and industry yield will likely be very enticing to long-term dividend investors. Meanwhile, the roughly 55% dividend payout ratio leaves ample room for adversity and should mollify all but the most conservative income lovers.

    Sources indicate that notably, the dividend has been increased regularly, though not annually, for over three decades. There have been no dividend cuts along the way despite the tech giant working through some difficult periods during that span. That indicates the board of directors is strongly committed to returning value to shareholders through a reliable, slowly growing dividend. Adding to the allure is the fact that the stock's 13x price-to-earnings ratio is notably below the pharma industry average of roughly 28x. The high yield and relatively low P/E ratio will likely be of interest to value investors.

    Growth investors will appreciate the above-highlighted success of the tech giant's growth portfolio. That portfolio is a collection of over a dozen new drugs that, as of the third quarter, account for nearly 60% of the company's drug revenues. That's good news and bad news, however, and it highlights the risk that investors face if they decide to buy Bristol Myers Squibb.

    The healthcare giant's legacy portfolio still accounts for around 40% of revenues, or roughly $5.4 billion. And one drug, Eliquis, is responsible for nearly $4.7 billion of that total. Eliquis is set to see generic competition as soon as 2028. When that happens, the revenue this drug produces will likely start to fall, and perhaps sharply. That is why investors remain downbeat on Bristol Myers Squibb's stock despite the success of its growth portfolio.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, it is reasonable that extremely conservative investors might want to stay on the sidelines until after Eliquis' patent expires. However, it is important to remember that patent expirations are just a normal part of the pharmaceutical business. And given the success of the growth portfolio, Bristol Myers Squibb continues to execute well in new drug development. There's just a mismatch between when patents expire, which happens on a set schedule, and its development efforts, which do not happen on a set schedule.

    It has been revealed that in order to buy Bristol Myers Squibb, you need to believe it will get through this period. History suggests it will, and that's backed up by the success of the growth portfolio.

    If you can't handle the uncertainty around the patent expiration of Eliquis, you shouldn't buy Bristol Myers Squibb. However, for most investors, including dividend, value, and perhaps even growth-focused types, the stock is probably worth a deep dive. The market doesn't appear to be giving the tech giant enough credit for its success on the development front, and that is probably tilting the risk-reward scale toward reward.

    Tech Report: The S&P 500 Has More Than Tripled in 10 Years, Even After Its Latest Pullback. Here’s What $1,000 in VOO Could Have Become.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (771 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From the start of 2026 to its peak on Oct.
    • Industry observers note that investors might be worried about a few things.
    • Recent findings suggest that step back.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    From the start of 2026 to its peak on Oct. 6, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%), the measuring stick for how the U.S. equity market is performing, posted a price return of 14%. Since that all-time high, though, the benchmark has fallen about 10% (as of Nov. 19).

    Industry observers note that investors might be worried about a few things. They could be more skeptical about all the artificial intelligence (AI) data center spending that's taking place. Elevated inflation and rising interest rates are stealing the show from a macro perspective. And we're past a midterm election cycle that saw the Democrats take control of Congress, introducing regulatory uncertainty.

    Recent findings suggest that step back. Even after its recent pullback, the S&P 500 index has risen 229% in 10 years. Here's what a $1,000 investment made in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) a decade ago could have become today.

    According to recent reports, the S&P 500 index climbed at a 12.6% annualized rate over the past decade, before dividends. Including dividends, a $1,000 investment in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF 10 years ago would be worth about $3,953 today. That's a 14.7% annualized total return. Investors almost quadrupled their money.

    In a recent development, the recent drop is a blip on the big-picture radar. Even after sliding since early October, the index is still up slightly in 2026.

    It has been revealed that what powered the gains? It's mostly earnings. In December 2016, the S&P 500 traded at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 17. This compares the index's price to the profits analysts expect over the next 12 months. Today, the multiple is around 18, slightly below its 10-year average.

    It has been revealed that based on this metric, the valuation barely moved. Forward earnings per share, meanwhile, jumped from $133 (at the end of 2016) to $416 in early November of this year, a 212% increase. Investors didn't make money by paying higher prices. They built wealth because American businesses became far more profitable.

    One sector stands above the rest. Information technology, measured by the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) delivered an annualized total return of roughly 22.7% in the last decade. AI, cloud computing, and surrounding internet-based secular trends made trillion-dollar market caps a common theme. The tech sector now represents 37% of the S&P 500 index. VOO investors own those winners automatically, for an expense ratio of just 0.03%.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, those gains weren't easy to hold on to. The S&P 500 index fell nearly 20% in late 2018, crashed 34% during the COVID-19 panic, slid 25% in the 2022 bear market, and dropped 19% during the 2025 tariff scare. This year alone has brought two declines of 8% or more. Volatility is just a part of the game.

    In a recent development, each time the market fell, selling felt like the right move. But each time, the index eventually bounced back and went on to new highs.

    It has been revealed that investors who trade in and out usually pay for it. Morningstar's (MORN -0.30%) latest Mind the Gap study found that the average dollar in U.S. mutual funds and ETFs earned 8.7% per year over the decade ended 2025. The funds themselves returned 9.9%. The difference is due to poorly timed buying and selling.

    It has been revealed that missing a few days hurts, too. According to J.P. Morgan (JPM -3.03%) Asset Management, sitting out the 10 best days over the 20-year period from 2006 through 2025 would have cut an investor's annualized return from 11% to 6.6%, an enormous difference.

    Dollar-cost averaging is the solution. This means investing a set amount on a regular schedule, regardless of price. There's no guessing involved. Adding steadily in this manner to the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF is no doubt one of the simplest ways to build wealth.

    When the market is down, like it is now, hang in there.The best results of the past decade came from holding through every pullback.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the stock market has had a rough few weeks.
    • Recent findings suggest that but according to Bloomberg reporting from Nov.
    • Industry observers note that goldman strategists predict that the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 points in the next 12 months.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ben Gran – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:44PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    It has been revealed that the stock market has had a rough few weeks. As of Nov. 20, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) had declined by about 10.4% in the prior month, largely driven by investor worries over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index has declined almost enough to qualify as a bear market, with a drop of nearly 20% since its Oct. 6 record high.

    Recent findings suggest that but according to Bloomberg reporting from Nov. 13, Goldman Sachs (GS -6.71%) strategists are bullish on the S&P 500 for next year. Recent research from Goldman suggests that the benchmark S&P index will gain 26% in the next 12 months by November 2027, despite possibly lower earnings growth compared to 2026.Let's look at what this might mean for investors -- and why it's a good sign to keep buying stocks with low-cost index funds like S&P 500 ETFs.

    Industry observers note that goldman strategists predict that the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 points in the next 12 months. On Nov. 20, the index closed at about 6,910, so this would imply a gain of about 26% from that level.

    That's not an outlandish return to expect for the S&P 500. A 26% gain in 12 months would be an exceptionally strong year, much better than the average. But it's well within the realm of possibility.

    Keep in mind that the long-term average annual return for the S&P 500, based on historical data since 1928, is 9.98%. And in the past few years, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) has delivered annual returns of about 17.8% in 2025, 25% in 2024, and 26.3% in 2023.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that why does Goldman think the S&P 500 will do so well in the next 12 months? If so many investors are nervous about tech companies spending too much on AI data centers, isn't now a bad time to buy the S&P? After all, as of Nov. 19, eight of the top 10 holdings in the S&P 500 were tech names, and those top eight stocks made up about 33.5% of the index by weight.

    The answer is in the valuations.

    Recent findings suggest that recent investor skepticism about AI stocks might actually be healthy for future returns. Recent declines in tech stock prices have driven down those companies' valuations. Goldman's research finds that AI hyperscalers are trading "well below" their historic valuations and says that "we see Technology -- and Hyperscalers in particular -- as relatively defensive.".

    It has been revealed that the very same tech stocks that have been going through a correction in the past month might be poised for bigger gains in the next 12 months. Goldman claims that even though some of the biggest hyperscalers have negative cash flow due to their aggressive AI investments, these companies still have strong balance sheets and could become attractive in the next 12 months if growth opportunities elsewhere are harder to find.

    Sources indicate that this trend of lower valuations can also be seen if you look at the S&P 500 index forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E). This metric demonstrates the index's earnings multiple based on the next 12 months' estimated earnings. The S&P forward P/E has dropped from a recent high of 30 to 21.08, trading at about a 15% discount compared to its five-year average.

    S&P 500 P/E Ratio Forward Estimate data by YCharts.

    Long-term investors need to think beyond today, tomorrow, or even the next 12 months. One year is not "long term." But this Goldman Sachs research is a helpful sign that there are many reasons to be optimistic about the stock market, despite some recent volatility.

    According to recent reports, if you share Goldman's optimism about the S&P 500 in 2027, now can be a good time to buy low-cost index funds like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO). This ultra-low-cost ETF lets you track the performance of the S&P.

    You don't have to pick stocks or worry about which companies or industries are winning or losing; this Vanguard ETF lets you own 500 of the largest publicly traded companies in America, representing about 80% of the total U.S. stock market. If Goldman's analysis is on target, your investment in the ETF could go up by 26% in the next 12 months.

    But even if that forecast doesn’t come true, you can rest assured that the S&P 500 has delivered strong average annual returns of about 10% for long-term investors who can buy and hold through temporary ups and downs along the way.

    When our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 768%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 199% for the S&P 500.

    #27704. Some FHA borrowers pay mortgage insurance for a decade or more. There's an industry push to change the rules

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (965 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Some FHA borrowers pay mortgage insurance for a decade or more. There's an industry push to change the rules

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Homeowners with conventional loans who pay mortgage insurance typically can shed that expense — meant to protect a lender against loss if the borrower defaults — once they've built sufficient equity in their home.
    • A fresh push to change the rules governing mortgage insurance for FHA loans came this week, after the Department of Housing and Urban Development released a report to Congress on Monday showing that the FHA's mortgage insurance fund remains financially strong.
    • Sources indicate that "The program's financial strength provides an opportunity for targeted changes that improve affordability for borrowers while preserving the long-term stability" of FHA's insurance fund, said Bob Broeksmit, president and CEO of the Mortgage Bankers Association, in a statement released after the report was issued.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Homeowners with conventional loans who pay mortgage insurance typically can shed that expense — meant to protect a lender against loss if the borrower defaults — once they've built sufficient equity in their home. But that's not how it works for those with a Federal Housing Administration loan.

    A fresh push to change the rules governing mortgage insurance for FHA loans came this week, after the Department of Housing and Urban Development released a report to Congress on Monday showing that the FHA's mortgage insurance fund remains financially strong. Its capital ratio — a measure of its financial cushion against potential losses — was 10.29% as of Sept. 30, down from 11.47% a year earlier, but still more than five times the 2% minimum required by Congress.

    Sources indicate that "The program's financial strength provides an opportunity for targeted changes that improve affordability for borrowers while preserving the long-term stability" of FHA's insurance fund, said Bob Broeksmit, president and CEO of the Mortgage Bankers Association, in a statement released after the report was issued. The trade group was one of a handful of organizations that put out statements calling for changes.

    The push, which revives a longstanding mortgage industry request, also comes several weeks after President Donald Trump issued an executive order that included calling for the launch of a federal pilot program that would cancel mortgage insurance on certain conventional loans once borrowers meet equity requirements.

    The order would apply generally to future loans backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac — two government-sponsored enterprises that purchase qualifying mortgages from lenders and resell them as bundled securities. It wouldn't apply to FHA loans.

    Recent findings suggest that FHA mortgages are issued by private lenders but insured by the federal government, which protects lenders against losses if a borrower defaults. The loans are designed to make homeownership more accessible, particularly for borrowers with limited savings for a down payment or with lower credit scores.

    Affordability challenges persist in the housing market, with elevated home prices and mortgage rates putting homeownership out of reach for many prospective buyers. Existing homeowners are also facing rising costs alongside their mortgages, including property taxes and homeowners insurance amid overall high inflation.

    About 83% of new FHA purchase loans went to first-time homebuyers in the most recent fiscal year, according to the FHA report to Congress. Altogether, the FHA insured more than 8.4 million mortgages as of Sept. 30.

    The median age of first-time buyers is 40, according to a new report from the National Association of Realtors.

    FHA loans also require borrowers to pay mortgage insurance regardless of the size of their down payment. Under current rules established in 2013, FHA borrowers with a down payment that's less than 10% of the loan must pay mortgage insurance premiums for the duration of the loan. Those who put 10% or more down pay that insurance for 11 years.

    Industry observers note that borrowers generally pay both an upfront mortgage insurance premium and an annual premium, which is typically divided into monthly payments. The upfront premium is usually 1.75% of the base loan amount and can be financed into the mortgage. For many borrowers with 30-year FHA loans, the annual premium is 0.55% of the outstanding loan balance.

    Conventional mortgages generally don't require mortgage insurance unless the loan is for more than 80% of the home's value. In 2022, the premium typically ranged from 0.58% to 1.86% annually, according to Fannie Mae.

    If those borrowers have to pay mortgage insurance, they can typically request its removal once they've built 20% equity in the home, or it is automatically canceled when their loan drops to 78% of the original value.

    The mortgage industry has floated two different proposals.

    It has been revealed that one would reduce the rate that applies to FHA mortgage insurance. For example, the Mortgage Bankers Association recently suggested a rate reduction of 20 basis points, which would lower the standard 0.55% rate to 0.35% for upcoming borrowers.

    For example: On a $350,000 mortgage, a 0.55% rate generally translates into $1,925 annually, or about $160 monthly, at the start of the loan. As the principal owed slowly goes down over time through a borrower's monthly payments, so does that mortgage insurance amount.

    At 0.35%, the annual premium would be $1,225 at the start of the loan, or $102 monthly — a difference of $58 per month.

    In a recent development, the FHA last cut that rate in 2023, when it was reduced from 0.85%. At the time, HUD estimated that affected borrowers would save an average of $800 annually. However, in the FHA's new report to Congress, the agency noted that the 2023 cut has reduced the fund's revenue, contributing to a decline in its capital ratio.

    The other industry proposal would implement auto-cancellation of premiums once the loan balance fell to 78% of the home's original value at purchase — in other words, the same as for Fannie- and Freddie-backed mortgages.

    "Cancellation prevents the squeeze for borrowers who have paid down their loans and shouldn't be paying for coverage they have outgrown," said Michael Farrell, president of the National Association of Mortgage Brokers, a trade group that generally has supported the cancellation proposal.

    "NAMB believes that cancellation at 78% protects the [FHA insurance fund], because premiums can restart if the [capital] ratio ever falls to 2%," Farrell noted.

    FHA mortgages received that treatment from 2001 through 2013, but the agency eliminated it to shore up its insurance fund after financial reserves deteriorated over time following the housing market crash, which led to the 2008 financial crisis.

    Sources indicate that whether the proposals will go anywhere this time is uncertain. HUD, which oversees the FHA, did not respond to a CNBC email seeking more information.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (326 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: White House replaces cyber director Sean Cairncross amid widespread tech outages

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (326 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that white House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, with Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies set to serve as acting director after a week of high-profile U.S.
    • The role, which advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates U.S.
    • Axios first reported Cairncross' exit, citing two White House officials who said President Donald Trump's chief of staff, Stephen Miller, pushed for his departure.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that white House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, with Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies set to serve as acting director after a week of high-profile U.S. technology outages.

    The role, which advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates U.S. cyber policy across federal agencies, has been handed to Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, on an interim basis. A permanent national cyber director must first be nominated by the president and then confirmed by the Senate.

    Axios first reported Cairncross' exit, citing two White House officials who said President Donald Trump's chief of staff, Stephen Miller, pushed for his departure.

    In a recent development, the White House declined to comment. However, a source familiar with the White House's thinking told CNBC that the President fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position because he lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job. Davies has the credentials to excel in the position and has been Senate-confirmed, the person added.

    The Office of the National Cyber Director did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment.

    It comes after a series of technology outages, including a nationwide aviation ground stop, a worldwide Microsoft Outlook outage and a reported blackout of the National Security Agency's classified communications network.

    The White House has insisted that there are no indications of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity or malign actor behind recent tech outages.

    Davies addressed her responsibilities in the upcoming position and thanked Miller and Trump for their confidence late Thursday.

    "Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected. Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come … but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on," she wrote on X.

    Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both congratulated Davies on her appointment.

    #27681. Bitcoin sell-off: Crypto is failing the 'digital gold' test again as it sinks with stocks

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1612 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Bitcoin sell-off: Crypto is failing the 'digital gold' test again as it sinks with stocks

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bitcoin's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned.
    • Coming into 2026, experts remarked that showing bitcoin could serve as a market hedge rather than a risk-on asset that moves up and down with growth stocks was an notable test for the cryptocurrency.
    • Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bitcoin's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned.

    Coming into 2026, experts remarked that showing bitcoin could serve as a market hedge rather than a risk-on asset that moves up and down with growth stocks was an notable test for the cryptocurrency.

    Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year. Its downward spiral in recent months and weeks has been precipitated by a confluence of factors. The heavy midterm elections losses for the Republicans, the Binance hack, and a world on edge about the security of all things technology — FAA ground stop, the outage of the National Security Agency's highly classified internal communications system, several online banking outages — have not helped the mood when it comes to putting trust in the digital world.

    But the market itself may be the biggest factor. Investors are currently in sell everything mode, including tech stocks and gold — the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 tumbled into correction territory on Friday, according to CNBC data. Bitcoin's recent price action has also tracked the move in the biggest tech IPOs, SpaceX and Anthropic. Taken together, the cryptocurrency is failing the test again when it comes to showing its worth as a market hedge during times of investor anxiety.

    In the past month alone, bitcoin had dropped roughly $20,000, as of Friday morning, according to CNBC data.

    Investors and financial management firms aren't viewing it as safe an investment as in the past, said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and chief executive of Global Settlement Network, a Miami-based fintech that provides infrastructure for currency settlement, including crypto. "There's a bit more caution than there was a year ago.".

    What is behind bitcoin's fall, and what is in store for its future? Here is what experts say.

    Sources indicate that there have been many theories about how bitcoin would react based on different market and economic conditions. But historically, bitcoin has done best in low-rate environments and when lending opportunities are plentiful, noted Juan Xavier Sanchez, head of wealth strategy at Activest Wealth Management in Aventura, Florida.

    When rates are down and treasuries aren't paying good yields, people tend to be more risk-seeking for higher returns. "Bitcoin for many investors is in that bucket," Sanchez said.

    Experts have noted that gold, which is now down over 35% from its early 2026 peak, is less attractive when cash accounts are paying 5%. Investments like gold and bitcoin offer no yield.

    Bitcoin's rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 since late September suggests the two are increasingly moving in tandem, according to data from Fairlead Strategies, a technical research firm. That's consistent with an environment of higher volatility in which correlations across risk assets tend to increase. However, the correlation remains below its early-2026 highs, the data show.

    Bitcoin has certain characteristics of digital gold, in that it has a limited supply, no single owner and no CEO or board that can decide to issue more, remarked Anthony Georgiades, founder and general partner at Innovating Capital in Newly introduced York, which invests in early-stage crypto, blockchain, digital infrastructure and deep tech companies.

    But it's also been caught up in monetary policy since its inception. The last decade or so of monetary policy has been extremely rewarding to speculative risk-on assets, Georgiades said. However, in periods of volatility, those types of assets have experienced the most significant drawdowns and have been the most heavily punished, Georgiades said. That means that a shock on one side of the board that might be completely independent of bitcoin could trigger a large volatility event "given how intertwined digital assets have become in the overall financial system," he said.

    In a recent development, notably, bitcoin hasn't acted much like digital gold in more recent years, noted Abe Sheikh, chief investment officer of Cordoba Advisory Partners in Upcoming York. In fact, it has fallen substantially during periods when the stock market has been falling. For example, from October 6 through November 18, the S&P 500 fell about 6.3%, and bitcoin fell around 27%. From January 21, 2025 through April 8, 2025, the S&P dropped around 17.4%, while bitcoin slid 27.8%, he said.

    Democrats gaining control over both houses is viewed as a negative for crypto from a market perspective. The crypto industry spent more than $200 million to support crypto-friendly candidates, but its role had less of an impact on overall results than in the last election cycle. However, bitcoin's downward trend was already in the works, remarked Cyrus Amini, chief investment officer at Hyphen Wealth Management in Lafayette, California.

    In September, the Clarity Act failed in the U.S. Senate, and while its outlook is now dim, according to many political and market experts, some form of crypto legislation is still considered a priority for many Democrats and Republicans, while the Trump-appointed heads of the Commodity Future Trading Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission continue to favor crypto in rulemaking.

    It has been revealed that this fall, investors also started to question the security of encryption technology, leading to more concerns over the security of their bitcoin holdings, mentioned Kirkley of Global Settlement Network. The Binance hack in October muddied the waters further. And the recent stock market jitters and economic concerns piled on doubts, Kirkley said. The last few weeks have been especially rough with data security concerns from multiple fronts, he added.

    Wall Street's embrace of bitcoin has been a big positive for the cryptocurrency. Kirkley noted that 20% of bitcoin's market price is coming from institutional investors, and that's a conservative estimate.

    In addition, newly introduced research from digital assets organization Galaxy shows that a record 40.5% of all 13F-reported spot bitcoin exchange-traded product holdings, and 11.2% of all the bitcoin in the funds, came from advisory and wealth planning firms, such as RIAs and brokerage platforms, as of the third quarter 13F filings with the SEC, which are required of firms with over $100 million in assets to report their holdings.

    Recent findings suggest that much of this investment is through bitcoin spot ETFs like the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) that track its price. These ETFs, first approved by the SEC in January 2024, were supposed to provide a reliable new source of institutional demand. But ETF ownership also makes bitcoin especially easy to sell.

    According to recent reports, outflows from several of these funds have been substantial in recent months. IBIT, the largest of its peers, had six-month net outflows of $1.65 billion through Nov. 18 and one-month outflows of $1.37 billion, according to ETF Database. The second biggest, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) had one-month net outflows of $322.65 million and six-month net outflows of $771.86 million, according to ETF Database. Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF (BTC) had one-month net outflows of $66.35 million, though it had inflows of $590.04 million over six months.

    As of September 2026, public companies collectively hold close to 1.29 million bitcoins, which is more than 6% of the 21 million coins in existence, according to bitcoin.com.

    Sources indicate that most public companies invest their corporate treasury portfolios in low-risk, highly liquid instruments such as money market funds, Treasury bonds and Treasury bills. That stated, there are some well-known companies that have invested in bitcoin. SpaceX, for example, purchased 18,712 bitcoins for a total cost of $661 million, at an average price of $35,324 per coin. The manufacturer began accumulating bitcoin in early 2021 and held its position unchanged from mid-2024 until its IPO filing.

    Digital Asset Treasury companies, known as DATs or DATCOs, have also played a role in bitcoin's volatility. DATs are publicly listed firms whose primary business strategy involves holding significant quantities of digital assets, such as bitcoin or ethereum, on their corporate balance sheets to drive shareholder value. Companies in this space include Strategy, Strive, and Twenty One Capital.

    "DATs have exacerbated the problem," mentioned Sheikh of Cordoba Advisory Partners. When bitcoin is rising, these companies borrow money in the debt market or raise capital to buy more bitcoin, which magnifies the upswings. They have also sold bitcoin to make their bond coupon payments. "It leads to enormous volatility on the upside and downside," Sheikh said.

    According to recent reports, as of mid-November, Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, holds 850,849 BTC, according to a regulatory filing. That represents roughly 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The company acquired these holdings at a total cost of approximately $64.2 billion, with an average purchase price of roughly $75,452 per coin, according to the filing.

    Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025. A trading range has taken hold and the bottom of the range is just below 60,000, mentioned Katie Stockton, founder and managing partner of Fairlead Strategies. "It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said.

    It has been revealed that oversold conditions on the heels of recent lows in June and July, in addition to long-term momentum, suggest bitcoin can support an upturn, she said. But that depends on whether the crypto can hold at a current range around $60,000, she said. "At the end of the day, bitcoin is exceptionally volatile. It's still an area that people might go to sell when they think that risk is higher in other areas.".

    Industry observers note that by mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July. It was on pace for its seventh-straight weekly loss for the first time since May 2022, according to CNBC data.

    #27676. Bitcoin's regulation bull case is played out. What could drive crypto gains moving forward

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (749 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Bitcoin's regulation bull case is played out. What could drive crypto gains moving forward

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S.
    • According to recent reports, bitcoin traded around $61,500 on Friday, a more than 50% decline from its all-time high above $126,000 reached in October 2025.
    • Investors now see Wall Street's embrace of blockchain technology — particularly tokenization — as the next trend to give bitcoin a boost.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026.

    According to recent reports, bitcoin traded around $61,500 on Friday, a more than 50% decline from its all-time high above $126,000 reached in October 2025. The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September.

    Investors now see Wall Street's embrace of blockchain technology — particularly tokenization — as the next trend to give bitcoin a boost.

    "Every single traditional firm is now looking at digital assets," BitGo CEO Mike Belshe told CNBC last week in an exclusive interview from the fintech-focused Cantor Convergence conference in Miami Beach. That includes BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager.

    He pointed to statements from the asset management giant's CEO, Larry Fink, who mentioned the next major evolution in global finance is the creation of digital representations of every stock, bond, fund and real-world asset onto a shared blockchain ledger.

    "I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference. He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO.

    Sources indicate that "First day of trading, we distributed it to our retail clients, and it started trading 24/7, and that's all because capital markets are now copying crypto markets and are sitting on the same rails," Assia mentioned. "Crypto markets have always been 24/7, they never sleep, and now what we're seeing is that capital markets are copying crypto markets using the same technology so stocks are moving onchain, they're being tokenized.".

    It has been revealed that assia stated that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto.

    In a recent development, he pointed to the CFTC earlier this month clearing the way for crypto-style perpetual futures tied to individual stocks to trade on regulated U.S. exchanges for the first time. Assia also highlighted the SEC's move to matter an order in September, creating a regulatory pathway for certain trading venues to trade tokenized representations of publicly traded U.S. stocks.

    It has been revealed that "Blockchain technology is now starting to power what's happening in capital markets," Assia told CNBC. "That is the one of the biggest changes we're going to see in capital markets for many, many years.".

    "We're talking about hundreds of trillions of dollars that are going to be tokenized and move onchain and at the same time, I do believe that will support prices of bitcoin and other blockchains as well," he continued.

    The industry is also watching whether inflation will ease and geopolitical tensions will subside in the new year, which could lower broader macro risk at the moment hampering the industry.

    Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway.

    According to recent reports, ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands. She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027.

    In a recent development, "Our macro forecast has inflation breaking down considerably," Wood told CNBC in an exclusive interview at Cantor Convergence. "I think the elections have increased our confidence there because the war [in Iran], one way or the other, is going to end.".

    She added that "bitcoin has weathered so much bad news," including the $6.3 billion Binance hack and the "distraction" of AI which, "many people would say is sucking the oxygen away from bitcoin.".

    The maturation of the artificial intelligence trade could provide an opportunity for bitcoin to find new inflows.

    Wood noted that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound.

    "I think if the Bitcoin and crypto world coalesces and makes investors feel that they've got their arms around security and actually understand that there might be more security issues in the traditional financial system, I think we're going to see a wave of support," Wood said.

    SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SpaceX's artificial-intelligence coding platform, Cursor, is considering moving away from using of Chinese AI models due to "geopolitical risk," CNBC has learned.
    • Cursor, which SpaceX acquired at an implied $60 billion equity value in August, had built its coding model Composer 2 on top of Chinese lab Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5.
    • firms that have adopted Chinese models, whose usage has spiked across the globe this year, worrying lawmakers in Washington.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SpaceX's artificial-intelligence coding platform, Cursor, is considering moving away from using of Chinese AI models due to "geopolitical risk," CNBC has learned.

    Cursor, which SpaceX acquired at an implied $60 billion equity value in August, had built its coding model Composer 2 on top of Chinese lab Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5.

    It's among the U.S. firms that have adopted Chinese models, whose usage has spiked across the globe this year, worrying lawmakers in Washington. The battle for AI supremacy between the U.S. and China has reached new heights in 2026 as Chinese models have improved.

    But now Cursor plans to "explore phasing out PRC [People's Republic of China]-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk," according to a report produced by the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Select Committee on China, shared exclusively with CNBC ahead of its publication on Friday.

    Sources indicate that the report, which follows a months-long investigation into the adoption of Chinese AI models into the American tech stack, said Cursor "informed the Committees" of those prepares. Airbnb and DoorDash also engaged with the investigation about their use of Chinese AI models.

    According to recent reports, spaceX declared it entered into a formal agreement to buy Cursor in June; the deal was completed in August. SpaceX is developing the Grok family of models, which Cursor has been involved in training.

    In a recent development, cursor, SpaceX and DoorDash did not respond to a CNBC request for comment. Airbnb declined to comment. The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    Recent findings suggest that the report found that cost, customization and near-frontier performance of Chinese AI models were driving adoption, with the U.S. lacking a competitive open-weight alternative at "price and performance the market demands.".

    "Beijing is now seeking to turn those technological gains into global market share and long-term dependence," the report indicates. China's embassy in the U.K. did not respond to a request for comment. China's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond.

    It also sets out recommendations to address the issues it has identified.

    Those include launching a "national American open-weight initiative" that combines public computing power, shared evaluation infrastructure and "lawful access" to American frontier models for training.

    The report also says an order, made public in October, that banned DeepSeek from federal civilian agency systems, should be built on, by prohibiting the use of "PRC-developed AI models" in federal information systems and in performance of federal contracts.

    Separately, Washington is also concerned about Chinese companies accessing Nvidia chips remotely, via overseas data centers, and gaining ground by using "distillation," where newly introduced models use older, more established ones to help train them.

    Industry observers note that the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, confirmed on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
